preconditions.expression: stdin.strip().split() != [] and all(c.isdigit() for c in stdin.strip().split())
preconditions.description: The first line of stdin contains exactly one integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 200000) representing the number of intersections.

preconditions.expression: len(stdin.strip().split()) == 2 and all(1 <= int(x) <= 200000 for x in stdin.strip().split()[1:])
preconditions.description: The second line of stdin contains exactly n integers a_1, a_2, ..., a_n where for each i (1 ≤ i ≤ n), i ≤ a_i ≤ n and a_i ≤ a_{i+1} for all i < n.

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip().split() != [] and len(stdout.strip().split()) == n and all(0 <= int(x) <= 200000 for x in stdout.strip().split())
postconditions.description: The output is a single line containing exactly n integers m_1, m_2, ..., m_n, where m_i is the minimum energy required to reach intersection i from intersection 1.

postconditions.expression: all(m_1 == 0) and all(m_i == min(sum(abs(p[j] - p[j+1]) for j in range(len(p)-1)) for p in paths_to_i) for i in range(1, n+1))
postconditions.description: For each intersection i (1 ≤ i ≤ n), m_i is the minimum total energy over all possible paths p_1=1, p_2, ..., p_k=i, where the energy is computed as the sum of |p_j - p_{j+1}| for normal steps, except when p_j + 1 = a_{p_j} and a_{p_j} ≠ p_j, in which case the step costs 1 unit instead of |p_j - p_{j+1}|.

postconditions.expression: all(m_i <= m_j + abs(j - i) for i in range(1, n+1) for j in range(1, n+1) if i != j)
postconditions.description: The computed m_i values satisfy the triangle inequality with respect to the energy metric, accounting for shortcuts.
